teaser.text: An electric pump may look like one machine, but its work depends on several specialized chips. Microchip Technology sells those chips and the supporting technology, so its business is easiest to understand by following one dollar from design choice to shipped part.

stock.title: Microchip stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Microchip stock forecast: weighted scenarios, recovery drivers, real free cash flow and valuation in plain English.
stock.opening: Microchip's weighted scenario is $53.28 in October 2027 and $74.59 in October 2029, after a −25% return including dividends and an +8% return. It hinges on end demand outrunning replenishment, margins holding after temporary benefits fade, and cash reducing debt.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Microchip's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Microchip's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s weighted path is weak at first, then recovers. By October 2027, the weighted price is $53.28, a 25% loss including dividends. By October 2028, it reaches $64.54, an 8% loss. By October 2029, it reaches $74.59, an 8% gain.
The terminal range is unusually wide. The bear case reaches $15.24 by October 2029. The bull case reaches $165.96, against today’s $73.85. The probabilities are 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Microchip, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires distributor restocking to fade before end-customer demand recovers. Low utilization and renewed inventory charges then suppress profit, while debt, preferred claims and dilution restrict cash for common shareholders. The bear case gives $20.57 in October 2027 and $15.24 in October 2029. Its 30% probability reflects 175 company inventory days, prior capacity charges and the business’s sharp cyclicality.

The bull case requires sell-through to exceed replenishment, new PCIe and 64-bit designs to reach production, and factory loading to expand margins. Strong cash generation then supports debt reduction and buybacks. The bull case gives $96.45 in October 2027 and $165.96 in October 2029. Its 20% probability remains lower because design wins were not yet volume shipments and dividends recently exceeded free cash flow.

paragraphs.text: After $91.1 million of capital spending, free cash flow was $871.0 million. That was better than the preceding year but far below the fiscal 2023 peak, when equipment and facility spending was also much higher.

blocks.heading: How much does Microchip pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: Revenue went through a boom, a 42.3% fiscal 2025 contraction, and only a 7.1% fiscal 2026 recovery; sales remain far below the fiscal 2023 peak. Operating margin recovered to 10.4% in fiscal 2026 after falling to 6.7% in fiscal 2025. Real free cash flow per share was $1.13 against $1.80 of dividends paid per share.

paragraphs.text: The recent pattern is less comfortable. Dividends exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026, and Microchip acknowledged using borrowings to help finance quarterly dividends. Borrowing to preserve a dividend keeps today’s payment intact but leaves less flexibility tomorrow and adds interest costs. The table tracks free cash flow, shareholder payments, investments, asset sales, share issuance and debt issued or repaid.

The forecast holds the dividend at $1.82 per share in every case and every year. That matches the rate maintained through fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026, while common dividends exceeded free cash flow in both years.

blocks.heading: Did Microchip keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: There is evidence that Sanghi has delivered part of his undertaking: Fab 2 closed, inventories declined, and the August 6, 2026 results call reported results above guidance. The recovery remains unfinished, however. Shareholders should credit the operating improvements while asking whether the value created for each existing share exceeds the cost of management’s pay.

blocks.heading: What is Microchip's revenue and profit trend over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: The quarterly pattern is clearer. Revenue bottomed at $970.5 million in March 2025. By June 2026, it had reached $1,484.7 million after rising in every intervening quarter. The recovery is real, but sell-through will determine how much of it reflects final demand.

blocks.heading: What should Microchip watch in November?

paragraphs.text: Microchip schedules its September-quarter results call for November 5, 2026, at 5 p.m. Eastern. Investors should compare sales and earnings with guidance, then check whether receivables rose faster than profit or inventory began accumulating again.

December’s outlook will be more revealing. A strong quarter could reflect replenishment, favorable product mix, pricing or licensing. Continued demand with controlled inventory would offer better evidence of a lasting recovery. Debt reduction should be judged after dividends, equipment purchases and acquisition payments.
